query: Threat-model a web-reading assistant that can upload files. Trace hidden page instructions into proposed uploads and enforce scoped credentials and independent destination policies using harmless attack fixtures.
Our search tool returns text that looks like a system message. Map how it reaches the model and executor, then prove that source content cannot become authority or user authorization.
Review a multi-tenant assistant using server-wide API credentials. Identify confused-deputy paths and restrict tool identity so a low-privilege user cannot act as an administrator.

Design containment tests for poisoned tool descriptions and changed tool metadata. Verify origin and version, restrict capabilities independently, and measure whether malicious suggestions cause forbidden effects.

A retrieved document tries to write new preferences that instruct the assistant to reveal secrets later. Threat-model memory poisoning, preserve taint/provenance, and validate writes outside model instructions.

Review an agent file tool for traversal, symlink escape, drive-letter paths, and UNC destinations. Use typed operations and resolved allowlists, with sandbox tests proving denied paths cause no effects.

An assistant fetches user-provided URLs through a tool. Review redirects, resolved addresses, metadata endpoints, DNS rebinding, decompression limits, and how malicious response content reaches later actions.
Our agent includes credentials in error messages and model-visible tool payloads. Design scoped credential brokering, safe envelopes, redaction, and leak tests using synthetic secret markers.
Trace a forged approval in a retrieved attachment through summarization, planning, and proposed payment. Specify containment at each trust boundary and verify a legitimate task still succeeds.

Assess a research agent that can run shell commands and access the network. Replace unnecessary broad capabilities and test injection through tool arguments without using real secrets or destructive targets.
Audit a normal web login flow for cookie flags, account enumeration, password hashing, CSRF, rate limits, and dependency advisories. No model reads content or chooses actions in this system.

Build the executable permission and reserve-floor gate for model-proposed transfers. Trusted principal, atomic budget reservation, and current versions are known; focus on business-rule admission, not threat discovery.

Assemble safety and quality controls across agent input, proposals, execution, and output. Measure abstention and false blocking and identify coverage gaps; detailed attack-path analysis is already complete.
Design a human approval preview for external messages, with exact recipients, attachments, expiry, and cancellation. The threat model and deterministic enforcement are settled.
Evaluate an agent on a representative gold set containing ordinary and adversarial tasks. Calibrate semantic graders and severity-weighted release gates without redesigning security controls.
Specify memory retention, consent, provenance, deletion, and conflicting facts for a support assistant. There is no suspected attack; the request is runtime persistence ownership and lifecycle.
Define typed structured outputs for an advisory model classifier, including refusal and missing evidence. Focus on supported schema constraints, semantic checks, and bounded formatting repair.

Our fixed agent integration needs deterministic tests for malformed proposals, denied effects, tenant isolation, and restart behavior. Implement the risk-based test matrix using existing security policy.
Profile retrieval and model-call latency in an assistant. Compare caching and smaller-model routing with fixed permission and quality gates; do not conduct a new threat assessment.

Add redacted telemetry and protected evidence references to existing agent traces. Verify run reconstruction and retention using established privacy rules, keeping the security architecture unchanged.
